q8.answer: Two layers. Staging is deduplicated to the latest updated_at per order_id (row_number over order_id ordered by updated_at DESC). The MERGE on order_id only updates a matched row when s.updated_at >= t.updated_at, so an older overlapping or re-run copy cannot overwrite a newer warehouse row. Equal timestamps just refresh identical data.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse, in the high_water_mark column of the etl_control row. It is set to max(updated_at) of the rows actually extracted, not the wall clock, and is unchanged if the extract was empty. It is written inside the same transaction as the merge and the run_log success update, immediately before the COMMIT.

q10.answer: Atomic commit. The merge into orders, the HWM advance and the run_log success mark all happen in one warehouse transaction. Dashboards read only committed data, so they see either the previous complete state or the new complete state. Staging is separate and dashboards never read it.

q11.answer: A failed attempt rolls back, so orders and the HWM are untouched. Its staged rows are not deleted at failure. The retry uses a new attempt that re-reads the HWM and recomputes window_lo = HWM - 2 hours, so the window is the same as the failed attempt's. The retry's stage step deletes any existing stg_orders rows for its run_id before loading. Orphaned staging rows from a failed attempt with a different run_id are cleaned only by the 7-day housekeeping step. I did not explicitly decide whether run_id is reused or new per attempt.

q12.answer: For each mismatched order-creation day (created_at::date, within the last 30 days), it re-reads all of that day's rows from the replica into stg_orders under a reconcile run_id. One transaction then applies all mismatched days with the same guarded MERGE (updated_at >= target), so it is atomic. It never touches or moves the nightly HWM.
